# Actual starter source fixtures

Baseline: `049c502536c43f8cefb4d804fab987e6d1855f39`. These are upgrade inputs. Original migrations remain unchanged and use the current patched toolchain/dependencies.

`starterFixture(t, mode) StarterFixture` constructs a **clean source**: two legacy schools, valid private objects and no live outbox lease. Modes are `shared` (both schools on control/shared), `dedicated` (each school on its own pool), and `mixed` (east shared, west dedicated). Shared and control are intentionally the same starter DB handle. The helper returns explicit legacy school routes, control/dedicated handles, source IDs, blob/event references and native signatures. It inserts legacy placement pins using original pool-marker IDs; it never invokes evolving runtime routing, readiness, authentication or document services during construction.

`starterFixtureFaults(t, mode)` / `injectStarterFaults(t, fixture)` explicitly add missing/corrupt/malformed/unsupported/copied-path objects and active leases until 2100. Raw source checks test both profiles in all three SQLite modes. Existing identity/file reader assertions live in a separate compatibility test, so later v2 readers cannot prevent source fixture construction.

Schemas are executed through `bootstrap.Migrations()` and Goravel's native migrator, including actual jobs/failed_jobs Blueprint tables, control ledger, target receipts, identity, Students, enrollment and all 41 work-list DDL. There are 42 registered modules; Students uses its specialized register rather than a work-list table. No replacement CREATE statements are used to construct source tables.

`registrations.json` pins the **actual registered objects** from the baseline's complete control/east/west composition root: 137 ordered descriptors (native jobs plus 46 plans expanded onto their real targets). A test-only accessor reads each `*registered` value's signature, implementation, plan ID, connection/driver/legacy owner, ControlOnly flag, Up/Down SQL and the exact SQL/arguments emitted by `registered.apply`, including implicit receipt creation/marks. Native Blueprint jobs are pinned by signature/implementation and the original migration source hash. The verifier restores the original spelling of the one renamed Go import before comparing the bytes. Only the original placement plan's generated random pool ID is normalized. Fixture modes select the corresponding canonical nodes; PostgreSQL changes only the driver/control connection name and associated receipt signature arguments. Before any migration, actual registered originals must match exactly, including placement/order; future appended IDs are excluded. Regression mutations change real registered Down/ControlOnly/order and must fail validation.

`tables.json` independently annotates all 55 durable control tables / 47 dedicated tables with owner, classification, placement and legacy scope column. Post-migration introspection compares exact table sets, verifies declared owner columns and matches owner/classification to the human inventory. An unexpected table is rejected. Native SQLite internal tables and PostgreSQL sequences are not application tables.

PostgreSQL variants require `EDUPILOT_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN` and permission to create/drop disposable schemas. Each expected database/schema is captured from the handle that created the schema. **Before native migration or ledger DDL**, every actual Goravel named handle must report the same `current_database()` and `current_schema()`, with an owned `edu_platform_<16 hex>` schema. The native schema ORM must use the verified control handle. Each verified pool keeps one connection; the registered SQL/source snapshot forbids unreviewed SQL changing that routing. Wrong database/schema handles fail before the migration callback; an optional live PostgreSQL regression proves a second physical schema receives no sentinel DDL. URL/keyword DSNs and driver metadata carry the same isolated schema. Supplied search_path/public are never migration targets. Missing DSN is an explicit open gate.

`schools.json` has public fixture-only credentials: equal emails, distinct stable 32-character user IDs, independent bcrypt hashes/passwords, valid deterministic bearer references and future session expiry. No production secrets are included. Both schools share business record IDs across Students, placements and every work list. Fixtures include Unicode private names, archived students, noninitial versions, closed work items and a withdrawn placement. Original `(school,student,year)` retry uniqueness is checked against the actual schema.

Each school has pending/dead/published student lifecycle events, byte-exact v1 payloads and a published audit receipt; fault injection adds leased events. Stable school-prefixed event IDs respect the original pool-global PK. Cross-pool duplicate event IDs remain a later manifest ambiguity case.

`objects.json` stores independent checked-in legacy bytes/base64 with deterministic canonical-v4 UUID/path references. Clean construction writes valid text only. Fault injection adds corrupt checksum, absent external reference, correct-checksum unsupported body, malformed header and west's copied east bytes/ID. The reader must reject copied path-bound hashes. Format: `EDUPILOT-DOC/1\n` + 32 raw SHA-256 bytes of `UTF8(path) || NUL || body` + body. The fixture implements no decoder. Native marker pool IDs retain actual random behavior.

Run from repository root:

```sh
go test ./tests/architecture ./database/edumigrations -run 'TestTenantOwnershipInventory|TestStarterFixture' -count=1 -v
```

Tests change process-global framework configuration and must not run in parallel. Each test closes/drops only its own handles/schemas/files. A task-local GOCACHE may be used where the default cache filesystem is full.

Deliberate exclusions: infrastructure queue rows remain empty (only job is global control session expiry); enrollment/workspace event encodings are inventoried while student lifecycle payloads cover delivery states; remote S3 enumeration, all media types, hostile paths/symlinks and upload concurrency stay in their dedicated suites; client storage/caches, orphan/ambiguous mapping, process fencing, rollback, v2 activation and online moves are later tasks. A real missing-object preflight needs both enumeration and external reference reconciliation.
